task.title: balanced-brackets
task.statement: The brackets package exposes is_bracket (already implemented) and a stub is_balanced(s). Implement is_balanced(s) so that it returns True when the three kinds of brackets (), [] and {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, and False otherwise. Characters that are not brackets are ignored. The empty string is balanced. is_balanced must return a bool. Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change is_bracket or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: nested mixed brackets with other characters are balanced: '(a[b]{c})', 'f(x[0], y[1])'
TypeError when s is not a string

spec.restated_task: Implement brackets.is_balanced(s) in brackets/core.py to validate matching and nesting of the ASCII bracket pairs (), [], and {} while ignoring all other characters. Return a bool for every string, including True for empty strings and strings without brackets, and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve is_bracket, package exports, and existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept str instances, including str subclasses. Scan brackets in their original order: each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket, and no opening brackets may remain unmatched at the end. Ignore every character other than (, ), [, ], {, and }, including whitespace, Unicode characters, quotes, and backslashes. Quotes and backslashes do not escape brackets or create special parsing contexts. Return exactly True when these conditions hold and exactly False otherwise.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str; do not coerce inputs to strings or accept bytes or other iterables as strings.
TypeError: the call omits required argument s or supplies unsupported arguments, as dictated by the signature.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation unchanged: return True exactly when c is a str instance of length one containing one of the six ASCII bracket characters; otherwise return False.
error_cases: TypeError: the call omits required argument c or supplies unsupported arguments, as dictated by the signature.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket both continue to work.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
4. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}', and '())'.
5. Every closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket: '[)', '{]', and '[(])' return False, while '([]{})' returns True.
6. Unmatched brackets at either boundary or within the input cause False: '[', '{', ']', '}', '(()', '[](', and ')(' return False.

7. Removing all characters other than the six ASCII bracket characters does not change a string's result. Strings containing only ordinary text, whitespace, Unicode letters, or non-ASCII bracket lookalikes return True.

8. Quotes and backslashes do not suppress bracket processing: a string consisting of a double quote, an opening parenthesis, and a double quote returns False; a backslash followed by an opening parenthesis also returns False.
9. For every accepted string input, the result has type bool, including both balanced and unbalanced cases.
10. Non-string inputs raise TypeError, including None, True, integers, floats, bytes, lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets, even when empty.
11. Instances of str subclasses are accepted and evaluated under the same bracket-matching rules.
12. Repeated calls are independent: calling with an unbalanced string does not affect the result of a subsequent call with a balanced string.
13. is_bracket remains unchanged and returns True for each character in '()[]{}', and False for 'a', '', '((', and 1. Existing tests remain unchanged and pass.
out_of_scope: Changing is_bracket, PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE, or package exports.
Supporting additional bracket types, quote-aware parsing, escaping, or programming-language syntax.
Coercing non-string inputs or introducing third-party dependencies.

sealed_tests.notes: Covers matching order, ignored characters, exact bool and TypeError behavior, str subclasses, independent calls, signatures, and both package exports.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.
